correctness.rationale: The rank-three quotient has determinant \(\mathcal O_{Q^3}(2)\). The remaining relative quadratic is a symmetric map from the dual quotient to the quotient, so its determinant is a section of the square of that determinant line, namely \(\mathcal O_{Q^3}(4)\). Generic smoothness prevents the determinant from vanishing identically. Since \(Q^3\subset\mathbf P^4\) is quadratic, the discriminant is a scheme-theoretic \((2,4)\) complete intersection. Adjunction and the divisor exact sequence give the listed canonical and cohomological invariants; the arithmetic replay in the frozen verifier is consistent with the symbolic calculation.
risks: No smoothness, normality, irreducibility, or singularity classification is asserted.
